name: Shinglebrook
region_detail: Along a lesser woodland stream outside the principal timber roads.
site_type: settlement | Inhabited locations | Independent woodland hamlet and craft community.
history: Several families established the hamlet before the Edict of the East, making shingles from carefully selected timber and weaving baskets from the flexible growth along the stream. Their households gradually constructed a shared drying shed and a small footbridge to connect the two banks.
current_state: The inhabitants continue to sell shingles, baskets, wooden vessels, and other small manufactured goods to traveling merchants. They manage nearby woodland through customary agreements governing the cutting and replacement of trees. Trade is modest but dependable, and no immediate dispute or crisis threatens the hamlet.
inhabitants: A small population of human, halfling, and half-elven craftspeople and their families; occasional merchants, woodland travelers, and visiting relatives from other independent settlements.
danger_level: Low within the hamlet; ordinary woodland hazards along its approaches.
points_of_interest:
Cluster of timber cottages; shared drying shed; shingle-splitting benches; basketry workshop; footbridge; managed coppice; streamside communal washing place.

Unresolved elements: The names, personalities, and relationships of the residents; The precise extent of the hamlet’s customary woodland rights; Its eventual commercial relationships with the growing timber industry.
discovery: Along a lesser woodland stream outside the principal timber roads. Independent merchants purchasing finished woodwork know the hamlet. Travelers following the stream or asking for supplies may be directed there.
